name: AD - Living Off the Land Enumeration
description: Enumerate the AD environment using only built-in Windows commands and PowerShell cmdlets — no external tools required. Use when tools are blocked by AppLocker/AV or when operating stealthily. Covers host recon, WMIC, PowerShell downgrade, and firewall checks.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks

variations.label: WMIC Domain Enum
variations.command:
wmic computersystem get Name,Domain,Manufacturer,Model,Username,Roles /format:List
wmic ntdomain list /format:list
wmic useraccount list /format:list
wmic group list /format:list
variations.description: WMI-based domain enumeration using wmic.exe — fully native, produces no PowerShell logs

variations.label: PowerShell Downgrade (Evade Script Block Logging)
variations.description: Downgrade to PS v2 — Script Block Logging (Event 4104) only works in PS v3+. After downgrade, PS commands are not logged. Confirm version with Get-host showing Version: 2.0

variations.label: Env & History Recon
variations.command:
Get-ChildItem Env: | ft Key,Value
Get-Content $env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Powershell\PSReadline\ConsoleHost_history.txt
Get-ExecutionPolicy -List
variations.description: Dump environment variables (reveals paths, domain, username), read PowerShell command history (often contains passwords), and check execution policy per scope

variations.label: Host & Network Quick Check (CMD)
variations.command:
hostname
echo %USERDOMAIN%
echo %logonserver%
ipconfig /all
arp -a
route print
wmic qfe get Caption,Description,HotFixID,InstalledOn
variations.description: Basic host fingerprinting from cmd.exe — domain, DC name, network adapters, ARP cache, routing table, installed patches

examples.label: Full host info — OS, domain, hotfixes, RAM in one command
List installed patches — look for missing CVEs
Downgrade PS to evade Script Block Logging
Read PS history — often contains cleartext passwords or useful commands

notes:
=== WHEN TO USE LOTL ===
- AppLocker blocks external tools
- AV deletes dropped binaries
- You need to stay under the radar (fewer alerts than pulling in Mimikatz)
- Client restricts internet access from the host

=== PS DOWNGRADE NOTES ===
  powershell.exe -version 2 evades:
  - Script Block Logging (Event 4104) — only works PS 3.0+
  - Module Logging
  BUT: the downgrade itself IS logged (Event 400 in Windows PowerShell log)
  So a vigilant defender will see the downgrade attempt even if subsequent commands are dark

=== WMIC vs POWERSHELL ===
  wmic.exe: no PS logging, produces cmd.exe process only
  net.exe: same — totally native
  PowerShell: logged unless v2 downgrade

=== USEFUL LOTL AD QUERIES ===
  dsquery * -filter "(objectClass=user)" -attr sAMAccountName
  net user /domain
  net group 'Domain Admins' /domain
  nltest /domain_trusts
  ([adsisearcher]"(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user))").FindAll() Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 21 (Active Directory Introduction and Enumeration).

defense.why_it_works: Built-in Windows binaries (wmic.exe, cmd.exe, netsh.exe, net.exe) are signed Microsoft tools that appear in normal admin activity — they generate far fewer alerts than dropped offensive tools. PowerShell v2 pre-dates Script Block Logging, so downgrading silences PS-based detection. All these techniques leverage functionality that cannot be removed without breaking core Windows functionality.
defense.prerequisites: Any authenticated foothold on a Windows host. No special privileges needed for most enumeration (systeminfo, ipconfig, PS history read).
defense.impact: Full host and domain enumeration without triggering AV or script-based detection. PS history often reveals cleartext credentials or useful admin commands run by prior users.
defense.detection: Windows PowerShell log (Event 400/403) records PS session start/stop including version — downgrade to v2 is visible here. Sysmon Event 1 on wmic.exe with unusual command lines. EDR behavioral baselines flag wmic querying AD objects or net.exe enumerate domain users rapidly. PSReadLine history access can be detected by auditing file reads on ConsoleHost_history.txt via SACL (File Object Auditing 4663).
defense.artifacts: Windows PowerShell log (Event 400: HostVersion=2.0 shows downgrade). Sysmon process create for wmic.exe, net.exe. No network artifacts for local queries; LDAP traffic for AD-directed queries.
defense.prevention: Disable PowerShell v2 (Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root). Enable Script Block Logging + Transcription. Deploy WDAC (Windows Defender Application Control) to restrict wmic.exe usage. Restrict read access to PSReadLine history files. Enable enhanced PS logging via MDI/MDE.
defense.evasion: Use cmd.exe native tools (net.exe, wmic, nltest) instead of PowerShell to avoid PS logging. Downgrade to v2 if PS is needed. Query AD via ADSI Searcher (built-in .NET, harder to detect than PowerView). Space queries out to avoid behavioral anomaly detection.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# PS v2 still installed (check):
Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2
# State: Enabled -> downgrade available

# PSReadLine history contains cleartext creds (common):
Get-Content $env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Powershell\PSReadline\ConsoleHost_history.txt
# Example output: Invoke-Command -ComputerName DC01 -Credential (Get-Credential admin / P@ssw0rd!)
defense.secure_config:
# Disable PS v2:
Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root

# Clear PSReadLine history at session end (add to PS profile):
Remove-Item (Get-PSReadLineOption).HistorySavePath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

# Restrict PSReadLine history saves:
Set-PSReadLineOption -HistorySaveStyle SaveNothing

# SACL on history file to detect reads:
# icacls $env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\PSReadLine\ConsoleHost_history.txt /audit:Everyone:R
defense.misconfiguration: PowerShell v2 left installed (most Windows Server 2012R2+ systems have it by default). PSReadLine saves all commands to disk including those containing passwords. Script Block Logging enabled but v2 not removed — trivially bypassed.
